actuator_details: **The learned replacement for hand-crafted feature detection + matching — the modern successor to SIFT/ORB + nearest-neighbor matching**. SuperPoint (2018): a self-supervised CNN that detects interest points + computes descriptors in one forward pass (a learned successor to Harris corner detector corpus + SIFT corpus). SuperGlue (2020): a graph neural network with attention that matches two sets of features by jointly reasoning about the whole correspondence problem (vs. independent nearest-neighbor) — handles wide baselines, repeated structures, occlusions far better. LightGlue (2023): an adaptive, ~10x faster SuperGlue (early-stops easy image pairs). Foundational to: modern visual SLAM + visual localization + SfM (COLMAP corpus increasingly uses learned features), AR/VR relocalization (Magic Leap built it for their headset), robotic place recognition. Paul-Edouard Sarlin also co-led the 'GLOMAP' and 'GLACE' visual-localization work. The standard learned-feature-matching stack in modern geometric vision.
control_architecture: SuperPoint: self-supervised CNN detector+descriptor. SuperGlue: attention-based graph neural network for joint feature matching. LightGlue: adaptive early-stopping variant.
creator: Magic Leap + ETH Zurich; Paul-Edouard Sarlin + Daniel DeTone + Tomasz Malisiewicz + Andrew Rabinovich (SuperGlue/SuperPoint); Philipp Lindenberger + Marc Pollefeys (LightGlue)

Predecessor: DeTone et al. 'SuperPoint: Self-Supervised Interest Point Detection and Description'. CVPRW 2018. Successor: Lindenberger et al. 'LightGlue'. ICCV 2023. Open-source.

actuator_details: **The foundational parameter-efficient fine-tuning method — democratized model adaptation**. LoRA: instead of fine-tuning all of a model's weights, freeze them and inject small trainable low-rank matrices (ΔW = BA, where B and A are tiny) into the attention layers — train only ~0.1-1% of the parameters, get nearly full-fine-tuning quality. Drastically cheaper: a 70B model can be LoRA-fine-tuned on a single consumer GPU. LoRA adapters are tiny (megabytes), swappable, and composable. QLoRA (2023): combines LoRA with 4-bit quantization, fine-tunes 65B models on a single 48GB GPU. Foundational to: the entire open-source fine-tune ecosystem (every Hugging Face fine-tune, every Stable Diffusion corpus LoRA, every custom LLM), parameter-efficient robot-policy adaptation (fine-tuning a VLA foundation model — Pi-0.5 corpus, OpenVLA corpus — for a new robot/task uses LoRA-style adapters), and the 'one base model, many cheap specializations' paradigm. One of the most-used ML techniques of the 2020s.

actuator_details: **The IO-aware exact-attention algorithm that made long-context Transformers practical**. FlashAttention: computes the exact attention output but reorganizes the computation to minimize reads/writes between GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and on-chip SRAM — tiling + recomputation so the O(N²) attention matrix is never fully materialized. 2-4x faster, 10-20x less memory, enabling much longer context windows. FlashAttention-2 (2023): better parallelism. FlashAttention-3 (2024): exploits Hopper GPU features. Now built into PyTorch, every major LLM framework, and essentially every modern Transformer training/inference stack — every frontier LLM (GPT-4 corpus, LLaMA corpus, Claude, Gemini) and every modern VLA (Pi-0.5 corpus, OpenVLA corpus, RT-2 corpus) uses FlashAttention or a variant. Tri Dao also co-created Mamba (round-56 mamba-state-space-gu-dao-2023). One of the most-impactful systems-ML contributions of the 2020s.

control_architecture: Tiled, IO-aware exact attention with on-chip recomputation; minimizes HBM↔SRAM traffic.

actuator_details: **The open-source text-to-image foundation model**. Latent diffusion: diffusion happens in compressed VAE latent space (32x downsampled vs. pixel space), making training + inference 10-100x faster. CLIP text-conditioning. CreativeML Open RAIL-M license — first major foundation model released under open weights. Triggered the open-weights generative-AI revolution. Subsequent: SDXL (2023), SD3 (2024). Tens of millions of downloads; ControlNet + LoRA + countless fine-tunes. Stability AI (Emad Mostaque) provided compute + release; LMU Munich CompVis (Rombach + Blattmann) did the research. Foundational to diffusion-based robotics policies (Diffusion Policy corpus).

actuator_details: **The collaborative cross-embodiment robot-learning dataset — the 'ImageNet of robot learning'**. The dataset that made 'generalist robot policy' a tractable research direction. 200+ authors from 30+ institutions — one of the largest robotics collaborations ever.

actuator_details: **The leading Transformer-alternative architecture — linear-time sequence modeling via selective state spaces**. Mamba: a state-space model (SSM) where the state-transition parameters are made input-dependent ('selective') — letting the model selectively remember or forget information as it processes a sequence, the way attention selectively attends. Unlike Transformers (O(N²) attention), Mamba is O(N) in sequence length, with a hardware-aware parallel scan algorithm (Tri Dao's signature — he also did FlashAttention round-56). Matches or beats Transformers of the same size on language, audio, genomics — especially at very long sequences (millions of tokens). Builds on the S4 (Structured State Space Sequence) line (Gu et al. 2021-2022). Foundational to: the post-Transformer architecture research direction (Mamba-2, Jamba, Zamba, hybrid Transformer-Mamba models), and increasingly explored for long-horizon robot policies + world models (an SSM's efficient long-context handling is attractive for robots that process long sensor streams). The most prominent challenger to the Transformer's (corpus transformer-vaswani-2017) dominance. Albert Gu → co-founded Cartesia AI; Tri Dao → Together AI chief scientist.
control_architecture: Selective (input-dependent) state-space model; linear-time hardware-aware parallel-scan sequence processing.

actuator_details: **The open-weight frontier LLM lineage that disrupted the AI-cost narrative — and the first open-weight reasoning model**. DeepSeek AI (founded 2023 by Liang Wenfeng, spun out of the High-Flyer quant hedge fund). DeepSeek-V2 (May 2024): Mixture-of-Experts (corpus mixture-of-experts-shazeer-2017) with Multi-head Latent Attention. DeepSeek-V3 (Dec 2024): 671B-parameter MoE (37B active per token), claimed trained for ~$5.6M (a fraction of frontier-lab budgets) — challenging the 'frontier AI requires billions in compute' assumption. DeepSeek-R1 (Jan 2025): an open-weight reasoning model — trained primarily via reinforcement learning (GRPO) to produce long chain-of-thought (corpus chain-of-thought-wei-google-2022) before answering, matching OpenAI's o1 (corpus gpt-lineage) on math/coding/reasoning benchmarks, released under MIT license. The 'DeepSeek moment' (late Jan 2025) — a Chinese open-weight model matching closed US frontier models at a claimed fraction of the cost — triggered a ~$1 trillion single-day reaction in AI-related stocks and reframed the open-vs-closed + US-vs-China AI competition. Anchor of the open-weight frontier-model ecosystem alongside LLaMA (corpus llama-meta-2023).

prior_art_notes: The Genesis simulator (Genesis-Embodied-AI/Genesis, December 2024) is the most recent and highest-throughput academic-grade open-source physics engine for robotics simulation, published Apache-2.0 by a multi-institution academic collaboration. Anticipates with full architectural specificity: (1) GPU-parallelized robotics simulation at 43M-FPS scale — directly relevant to commercial claims on sim-to-real-at-scale humanoid IP (notably Genesis AI Inc.'s GENE-26.5 product, with which this open-source project shares a name); (2) unified multi-physics architecture (rigid + soft + MPM + FEM + fluid) — relevant to claims on multi-domain humanoid simulation; (3) differentiable simulation for gradient-based policy optimization — relevant to claims on policy-gradient humanoid training at scale; (4) the URDF/MJCF interoperability surface that permits OpenLoco-class descriptors to be simulated without modification. Modern claims on sim-to-real-at-scale, multi-physics simulation, or differentiable physics for humanoid training all face this 1.5-year-deep open-source academic prior art with full source disclosure under Apache-2.0.
